sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Interactive Lab 1: Cyber Forensics and Dwell-Time Simulator. Manipulate the infiltration vectors, adjust attacker dwell time and database record volume, and toggle architectural countermeasures to observe live Romanosky cost scaling and exfiltration containment.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Let's run the Forensics Lab! Try switching between the Equifax and Capital One presets to see how dwell time and envelope encryption transform the financial blast radius!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Formative Checkpoint 1: Equifax Expired Certificate and Detection Blindspot. Why did attackers dwell undetected for 76 days despite internal network intrusion sensors? Select the root operational cause.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Time for Checkpoint 1, Kaito! Think about what happens when deep-packet inspection sensors lose their internal decryption keys.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Spot on! An internal TLS inspection certificate expired 10 months prior to the breach, blinding network intrusion detection sensors to encrypted database traffic over 76 days of uninterrupted dwell time!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Not quite. The failure was not quantum decryption or a misconfigured public S3 bucket; Equifax's internal TLS decryption certificate on its packet inspection appliance had expired ten months earlier, blinding their intrusion sensors.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Interactive Lab 2: Enterprise Cloud Combinatorial Risk and Egress Entropy. Adjust multi-cloud storage bucket counts to observe combinatorial breach probabilities, and simulate network flow entropy drops during bulk exfiltration.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Check out Lab 2! Notice how just a 0.3 percent error rate per bucket makes a breach almost 95 percent certain across one thousand buckets, and see the Shannon entropy gauge trip the circuit breaker!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Formative Checkpoint 2: Capital One SSRF and the Sublinear Cost Paradox. Evaluate the mechanism of AWS IMDSv2 hop-limit enforcement and the mathematical basis of Romanosky sublinear power-law scaling.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Checkpoint 2! Combine what you learned about IMDSv2 session tokens and hop limits with the Romanosky sublinear scaling exponent beta equals 0.72.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Precisely correct! IMDSv2 enforces an IP hop limit of 1, causing forwarded SSRF proxy requests to be dropped, while Romanosky's sublinear exponent beta of 0.72 ensures that a 100-fold increase in records increases variable costs by only approximately 27.5 times!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. IMDSv2 stops SSRF by enforcing a session token and setting the IP hop limit to 1 so forwarded proxy packets drop. Economically, breach costs follow a sublinear power law with beta of 0.72, not linear multiplication.
